title: Plugin CI, hooks and managed settings
bridge: Plugin CI is like the CI of an npm library that every app in the company auto-updates to. A broken release reaches everyone at once, so the checks run before merge. Except: a plugin can also run code on every laptop (hooks, MCP servers) and change how agents behave. So CI also flags risky changes for the reviewer and proves with evals that the plugin helps.
intro: claude-plugins needs the same safety as any shared code, and a bit more. This lesson builds plugin CI, the secret scan and the high-risk flag. Then it adds rhino-core's two safety hooks, the eval gate, and the managed settings that put rhino-core on every laptop. The hooks and CI scripts are Python because python3 ships on every Mac with git's Command Line Tools, while Node does not.

sections.h: Plugin CI, part 1: triggers and outputs (G8-07)
p: Claude Code updates a plugin only when its version changes, and a broken manifest silently drops a skill on every laptop. Both are cheap to catch before merge. G8-07 adds .github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml to claude-plugins. It can also be called with workflow_call, so rnd-kb-tooling (kb) and fcp-local-lab (fcp-lab) run the same checks.
Pin Claude Code by version, and make plugin-ci / validate a required check in the ruleset.
sections.because: We publish the list of changed plugins as a job output, because the evals job runs only for those plugins.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml
name: plugin-ci
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_call: {} # rnd-kb-tooling (kb) and fcp-local-lab (fcp-lab) reuse the same checks
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest # needs no model access; confirm the runner group with DevOps
    outputs:
      changed_plugins: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.plugins }} # JSON list for the evals job (G8-12); nightly: every plugin

sections.h: Plugin CI, part 2: the three checks
p: scripts/check_skills.py is adapted from agent-skills' validate_frontmatter.py. It checks that name matches the folder (claude plugin validate does not, as the g8-1 lab showed). It checks that description plus when_to_use is under 600 characters and says when to use the skill. Claude Code truncates at 1,536.
It also checks that the skill is in catalog.yaml with an owner and has 3 to 10 eval cases under evals/<skill>/. It warns on ALL-CAPS MUST, NEVER or CRITICAL.

scripts/check_version_bump.py fails when anything under plugins/

sections.because: We validate the catalogs and every plugin separately, because a broken plugin manifest does not always break the catalog.

code.text:
steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with: { node-version: 24 }
      - run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.289 # pinned; Renovate bumps it
      - name: Validate the catalogs and every plugin
        run: |
          claude plugin validate . --strict
          claude plugin validate channels/latest --strict
          for plugin in plugins/*/; do claude plugin validate "$plugin" --strict; done
      - name: Skill frontmatter, description limits, owners and eval counts
        run: python3 scripts/check_skills.py --catalog catalog.yaml --min-cases 3 --max-cases 10
      - name: Version bumped for every changed plugin
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: python3 scripts/check_version_bump.py --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
      - id: changed
        run: python3 scripts/changed_plugins.py --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref || 'main' }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

sections.h: Secrets and the high-risk flag, part 1 (G8-08)
p: Hooks, MCP servers and scripts run code on every machine that has the plugin, and allowed-tools skips permission prompts. A Snyk audit found 13% of public skills with critical issues. So these changes need a careful look, and the reviewer must know which ones they are.

A second job, secrets, runs gitleaks from its pinned release binary over the PR's commits: gitleaks git --log-opts=origin/main..HEAD --redact --exit-code 1. gitleaks is a scanner that finds keys and tokens in git history. The risk job below finds the risky changes.
sections.because: We match paths and frontmatter lines, because a hook file and an allowed-tools line both change what runs unasked.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml (continued)
  risk:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - name: Find changes that run code or skip prompts on every machine
        id: risk
        run: |
          base="origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
          git diff --name-only "$base"...HEAD | grep -E '(^|/)(hooks|bin|scripts|monitors)/|\.mcp\.json$' > risky.txt || true
          git diff "$base"...HEAD -- '**/SKILL.md' | grep -E '^[+-](allowed-tools|disallowed-tools):' >> risky.txt || true
          echo "count=$(wc -l < risky.txt | tr -d ' ')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

sections.h: Secrets and the high-risk flag, part 2
p: The label informs the one reviewer; it is not an extra approval. The repo keeps exactly 1 approval and no CODEOWNERS. The reviewer runs the plugin locally before approving. Add to STYLE.md: prefer a skill that runs a CLI over a new MCP server. A new MCP server needs Ronen (Security) and an entry in the managed MCP allow-list (G8-16).
sections.because: We edit one comment in place instead of posting new ones, because each push would otherwise add noise to the PR.

code.text:
- name: Label and explain for the reviewer
        if: steps.risk.outputs.count != '0'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR" --add-label high-risk
          { echo "**High risk:** these changes run code or skip prompts on every laptop and agent VM with this plugin."
            echo "Please run the plugin locally before you approve."
            echo '```'; cat risky.txt; echo '```'; } > comment.md
          gh pr comment "$PR" --body-file comment.md --edit-last --create-if-none

p: A plugin's hooks live in hooks/hooks.json. They work like the hooks in lesson p8-4, but they run as commands on the person's machine. Before a write, guard_write.py refuses content that looks like a secret: AWS keys, GitHub and Slack tokens, private key blocks. It also refuses edits to credential files (.env*, *.pem, id_rsa*, **/secrets/**), with exit 2 and a short reason.

After an edit, lint_after_edit.py lints that one file. frontend/**/*.ts(x) gets npx biome check <file>. A .py file under cloud/, client/ or sdk/ gets black --check, isort --check and flake8 with the repo's config. Problems come back as context and never block.
Keep both to one file and a few seconds, and silent when clean. Two eval cases: writing a fake AWS key is refused; a .tsx edit with a lint error shows the Biome message.

Gotcha: the G8-09 matcher names MultiEdit, which the hooks docs we checked do not list. Check the hooks docs of your Claude Code version for the exact tool names. A name that matches no tool does nothing, so test that Write and Edit really trigger the hook.
sections.because: We write the hooks in stdlib Python, because they run from the plugin folder with no install step.

sections.h: The eval gate, part 1: where it runs (G8-12)
p: A skill can read well and still make results worse. G8-12 runs each changed plugin's eval cases in CI (lesson p12-3). PRs run the cases tagged pr, which use free graders only (no model calls to judge). The nightly, cron 23 2 * * *, runs every plugin and every case, including LLM-judge graders.

The runner is an ARC set inside inf with single-use pods, because the LLM gateway is internal. The runner holds no Anthropic key: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at the gateway, which adds the evals key. Install bubblewrap and socat in the runner image for cases that grant Bash.
sections.because: We run one matrix leg per changed plugin, because each plugin's suite is judged on its own.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml (continued)
  evals:
    needs: validate
    if: needs.validate.outputs.changed_plugins != '[]'
    runs-on: ai-agents-runner-set # ARC set inside inf that can reach the LLM gateway; name from G1/G3, confirm
    strategy:
      matrix:
        plugin: ${{ fromJson(needs.validate.outputs.changed_plugins) }} # nightly: every plugin
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.LLM_GATEWAY_URL }} # the gateway adds the evals key; the runner holds none
      CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL: medium
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
      - run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.289

sections.h: The eval gate, part 2: better than no plugin
p: claude plugin eval runs each case with the plugin and without it, the no-plugin baseline. Each case runs 3 times. The job fails when any case scores below 0.8, and also when the plugin does worse than no plugin. Models are pinned (agent claude-opus-5-5 at medium effort, judge claude-sonnet-5-5), so a model rollout is not mistaken for a plugin regression.

--trust-plugin is acceptable here, because the pod is single-use and holds nothing but gateway access. There is no --max-cost-usd: cost is reported (costUsd in the JSON) and charted in Grafana. A ceiling comes only after 4 weeks of data. Results go to the G1 eval store.
sections.because: We fail on a negative mean delta, because a plugin that makes agents worse must not reach every laptop.

code.text:
- name: Run the cases with and without the plugin (3 runs each)
        run: |
          tags=$([ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ] || echo "--tag pr") # PRs: free graders only
          claude plugin eval "plugins/${{ matrix.plugin }}" $tags \
            --trust-plugin --no-publish --json results.json \
            --model claude-opus-5-5 --judge-model claude-sonnet-5-5 \
            --threshold 0.8 --runs 3 -j 4
      - name: Fail if the plugin makes results worse than no plugin
        run: |
          jq -e '.aggregates.meanDelta == null or .aggregates.meanDelta >= 0' results.json \
            || { echo "::error::${{ matrix.plugin }} scores lower with the plugin than without it"; exit 1; }
          jq -r '.cases[] | select((.aggregates.delta // 0) < 0) | "::warning::\(.name) regressed by \(.aggregates.delta)"' results.json
      - name: Store results in the eval store (G1; AWS access through G1's OIDC role)
        if: always()
        run: aws s3 cp results.json "s3://${{ vars.EVAL_RESULTS_BUCKET }}/skill-evals/${{ matrix.plugin }}/${{ github.run_id }}.json"

p: Managed settings are Claude Code settings the organisation sets for everyone, which a person cannot override (lesson p12-2). They are the one way to give every engineer the same tested tools without asking each person. They also keep unreviewed marketplaces and MCP servers off company laptops.

Inventory first: on 5 laptops run claude mcp list and /plugin, and list the claude.ai connectors people use (Jira, Slack, Figma). allowedMcpServers also filters claude.ai connectors, so a missing entry cuts a tool people rely on. Decide the delivery with DevOps: the claude.ai admin console (one policy, Owner role) or Fleet MDM profiles. Fleet is the device-management (MDM) tool that pushes files and settings to company laptops (lesson p12-2). Force-enabled plugins cannot be swapped per person, so pilots need their own profile with rhino-latest.
sections.because: We list allowed marketplaces by repo pattern, because a pattern covers every catalog and channel we own without listing refs.

sections.h: Managed settings, part 2: MCP, models and telemetry
p: Decide the MCP list with Ronen. Rhino MCP is allowed on mcp-dev3 only, because prod reaches customer data and PHI never enters a prompt. Add the compliance connector from G6-13 and every connector the inventory found. The model and telemetry keys belong to G0 and G1; they sit in the same file because there is one policy.

Pilot on 3 people for 2 days: /status shows the managed source and /plugin lists rhino-core. Then everyone. For agents, the G3 image bakes the stable catalog into a seed folder (CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR) with the same policy file. So Nova runs what people run. Retire the claude.ai org copies of ticket-to-pr and fcp-lab.
sections.because: We allow only managed MCP servers by URL, because a hand-added server could reach data nobody reviewed.

code.text:
"allowManagedMcpServersOnly": true,
  "allowedMcpServers": [
    { "serverUrl": "https://mcp-dev3.example.com/*" },                // Rhino MCP on test data; prod reaches customer data
    { "serverUrl": "https://<compliance connector host>/*" },             // from G6-13 (Nave)
    { "serverUrl": "https://<each connector in the inventory>/*" }        // Jira, Slack, Figma: don't cut what people use
  ],
  "deniedModels": ["fable"],                                              // G0: Fable needs 30-day retention (a compliance call)
  "env": {                                                                // G1 owns this block
    "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY": "1",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT": "https://<otel collector on inf>",
    "OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS": "0",
    "OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS": "0"
  }
}

worked.do:
Put "PreToolUse" back. Create hooks/guard_write.py, a small version of G8-09's guard:

"""PreToolUse hook: refuse writing something that looks like a secret, or editing a credential file."""
import fnmatch
import json
import re
import sys

SECRET = re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[0-9A-Za-z]{36}|xox[bp]-[0-9A-Za-z-]+|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----")
CREDENTIAL_FILES = [".env*", "*.pem", "id_rsa*", "*/secrets/*"]

event = json.load(sys.stdin)
tool_input = event.get("tool_input", {})
path = tool_input.get("file_path", "")
text = tool_input.get("content", "") + tool_input.get("new_string", "")

if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(path.split("/")[-1], p) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) for p in CREDENTIAL_FILES):
    print(f"Refused: {path} looks like a credential file. Ask a person to change it.", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
if SECRET.search(text):
    print("Refused: the new content looks like a secret (key or token). Use an env var or Vault path instead.", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
sys.exit(0)
echo '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"src/config.ts","content":"const key = \"AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP\""}}' | python3 hooks/guard_write.py; echo exit=$?

Refused: the new content looks like a secret (key or token). Use an env var or Vault path instead.
exit=2

worked.do: echo '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"src/config.ts","content":"const key = process.env.KEY"}}' | python3 hooks/guard_write.py; echo exit=$?

lab.faded: Feed the guard an Edit of /repo/.env.local (tool_name Edit, tool_input with file_path, old_string and new_string). Predict the message and exit code; building the JSON line is left to you.
lab.alone: Add the PostToolUse entry from G8-09 to your hooks.json, pointing at hooks/lint_after_edit.py. Write that script so it reads the event, prints "lint: would check <file_path>" to stdout, and always exits 0. Validate the plugin with --strict, then pipe a fake Edit event into the new script.
lab.done: Your plugin passes validate --strict with both hooks, the guard refuses the fake key, and the lint stub never blocks.

quiz.q: A PR adds a new script under plugins/rhino-core/hooks/. What happens in plugin CI?

options.text: It needs two approvals instead of one.
options.why: The repo keeps exactly 1 approval; the label informs, it does not add an approver.

options.text: The risk job adds the high-risk label and a comment telling the reviewer to run the plugin locally.
options.why: Hooks run on every laptop and agent VM, so the reviewer must look closely.

options.text: It is blocked until Security approves.
options.why: Only a new MCP server needs Ronen; a hook change needs a careful reviewer.

quiz.q: A skill's eval cases score 0.9 with the plugin and 0.95 without it. Does the eval gate pass?

options.why: The threshold is one rule; the plugin must also not do worse than no plugin.
Any negative mean delta fails the job.

options.text: No, the plugin makes results worse than no plugin.
options.why: The meanDelta check fails the job and names the plugin.

quiz.q: Why does the managed policy list allowedMcpServers by URL and set allowManagedMcpServersOnly?

options.text: So only reviewed MCP servers run, and prod Rhino MCP, which reaches customer data, stays off.
options.why: PHI never enters a prompt; mcp-dev3 has test data only.

options.text: To make MCP servers start faster.
options.why: It is about which servers may run, not speed.

options.text: Because claude.ai connectors are not affected by this list.
options.why: They are, which is why the inventory comes first.
